title: Sparse Congruence-Preserving Perturbations of Dyadic Series
subject: Erdős #251
question: What tail-shift condition would prove irrationality in Erdős #251, which natural affine schedules provably cannot supply it, and what prime-gap input still survives?
precis: The paper identifies the complete prime-gap tails and classifies rationality by integrality of their shifts. Two adjacent shifts in (-1,1) with unequal associated gaps cannot both be integral, so their cofinal occurrence for every positive shift would prove irrationality. A positive even polynomial word has integral shifts everywhere, and a sparse rationalising perturbation of the actual prime gaps preserves every fixed eventual congruence and short-block empirical distribution while keeping small corrections. These countermodels delimit growth, parity, congruence, and local-statistics arguments; the prime-specific cofinal small-shift assertion remains open.
owns: the problem-specific exposition for Erdős #251: summation by parts, dyadic tail recurrences, integral-shift criteria, local certificates, order-lattice and factorial-diagonal structure, adaptive and fixed affine no-go theorems, and the remaining cofinal condition
